title: Can't build Flutter applications on old x86_64 CPUs with 3.16.0 and greater
body: I upgraded from Flutter 3.10, where development worked normally, to Flutter 3.16.3/3.16.4. Creating a new sample project now appears to stop after downloading sky_engine and exits with code 3221225501. Building for Windows fails through flutter_assemble with code 1 and exits with -1073741795. Removing the Windows folder, running flutter clean, and repairing or cleaning the Dart pub cache did not help. What is causing this exit code, and how can I build projects successfully again?

symptoms_visible: After upgrading from Flutter 3.10 to 3.16.x, flutter create appears to stop around downloading sky_engine and exits with 3221225501; Windows builds fail during flutter_assemble and exit with -1073741795.
Removing the Windows project folder, cleaning the project, and cleaning or repairing the pub cache do not change the failure.
N0.label: N0 Flutter tool exits on new projects

symptoms_visible: The suggested fixes from the linked MSB8066 Stack Overflow thread have already been tried, and flutter create and builds still terminate with the same exit codes.
N1_x.label: N1_x generic MSB8066 troubleshooting aftermath

symptoms_visible: Reinstalling and testing several Flutter SDK versions does not make Flutter 3.16.x work; its projects still fail to build.
N2_x.label: N2_x Flutter reinstall aftermath

symptoms_visible: Flutter 3.10.5, 3.13.0, and 3.13.9 work, while 3.16.0 and later fail on new projects across Windows, Android, and web.
Affected machines use older x86-64 processors including AMD Phenom II, AMD Athlon II, and Intel Core 2 Quad, and verbose output abruptly stops without a useful Flutter error.
N3.label: N3 version boundary and old CPUs established

symptoms_visible: Git bisects on affected machines identify first-bad Flutter engine-roll commits from July 12–13, 2023, placing the regression in the same narrow period.
N4.label: N4 regression localized by bisect

symptoms_visible: Running the one-line Dart floor test normally crashes with -1073741795 in the double floor path, while running it with --target-unknown-cpu prints 42.
CPU tracing on the affected AMD and Intel machines reports SSE2 support but no SSE4.1 support.
N5.label: N5 unsupported instruction isolated

symptoms_visible: On affected older processors, Flutter 3.19.5 with Dart 3.3.3 creates and builds projects successfully.
Users confirm that Windows and web runs succeed and that the double ceil test produces the expected result without crashing.
N6.label: N6 stable hotfix verified by affected users

symptoms_visible: The Dart CPU-instruction restriction fix is available in Flutter 3.19.5 stable with Dart 3.3.3, and affected users can build and run Flutter projects on their older x86-64 CPUs.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

solution.intent: Treat the Windows failure as a generic MSB8066/CMake project problem and apply the fixes from the linked Stack Overflow thread.
solution.concrete_example: Try the suggested MSB8066 remedies from the linked Stack Overflow thread, such as repairing the Windows build setup and regenerating project files.

edges.comment: Thread c0-c1: the reporter had already tried the linked MSB8066 suggestions and confirmed that none worked.

solution.intent: Replace the Flutter installation in case the SDK or its cache is corrupt.
solution.concrete_example: Install a fresh Flutter SDK and retry creating and running a new project.

edges.comment: Thread c2-c3: the reporter reinstalled and tested several SDK versions; reinstalling did not make the affected versions work.

question_patterns: Which exact Flutter versions work and which fail?
Does the problem occur only for Windows builds or on Android and web too?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Flutter 3.10.5, 3.13.0, and 3.13.9 work. Flutter 3.16.0, 3.16.4, and later tested releases fail, including new projects on Windows, Android, and web.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every tested Flutter version, including 3.10 and 3.13.9, fails in the same way on this machine.
Flutter 3.13.9 is the latest working stable release, while several different 3.16.x patch releases fail.

question_patterns: What processor is installed in the affected machine?
Do other affected users also have older CPUs?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The original machine has an AMD Phenom II X4 965. Other reporters reproduce it on AMD Athlon II, AMD Phenom II X6, and Intel Core 2 Quad Q6600 processors; these are older x86-64 CPUs that do not provide SSE4.1.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same failure is widespread on recent Intel and AMD processors that report SSE4.1 support.

question_patterns: Does the machine meet Flutter's documented Windows system requirements?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, I checked the linked requirements and the machine meets the documented requirements.

question_patterns: Can you run flutter run -v for Windows, Android, and web and share what happens?
Does verbose output show a Dart exception or another useful error before termination?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Verbose runs on all three platforms eventually terminate abruptly, often around a Flutter tool or artifact-processing step, without a useful Flutter stack trace explaining the exit.

question_patterns: Can anyone else reproduce the same version-dependent failure?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Several users with old AMD and Intel x86-64 processors report the same abrupt exit after upgrading, and downgrading to Flutter 3.13.9 restores operation.

edges.comment: Thread c3-c13 and c33: exact version behavior, cross-platform impact, system requirements, verbose logs, and the shared old-CPU characteristic were collected. Multiple affected users are folded into one simulated user side.

question_patterns: Can you git bisect the Flutter repository between a working 3.10-era commit and a failing commit?
Which Flutter commit first introduces the crash on the affected hardware?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Affected users completed bisects. They reported first-bad engine-roll commits 47ba59c762919d66811b72acab9732d6aa2a93c9 and ee4208fd26abd5c91680b4aa185df0ae9e00ce61, both from July 12–13, 2023. Although the exact roll differed, both results localized the regression to the same narrow period.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The bisect points to a Flutter framework UI change with no Dart or engine roll nearby.
A repeat bisect identifies a neighboring engine-roll commit from the same day.

edges.comment: Thread c37-c45: two affected users completed the requested bisection. Their exact first-bad commits differed but were adjacent in time and both were engine rolls; contributors are merged into the simulated user side.

question_patterns: Using the Dart executable bundled with Flutter, what happens when you run a one-line program that prints 42.0.floor()?
Can you run the floor.dart reproducer and share the crash details?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Running main() { print(42.0.floor()); } with the bundled Dart executable crashes with ExceptionCode -1073741795. The stack points into the double floor path, and debugging identifies the SSE4.1 roundsd instruction.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The normal Dart command prints 42 successfully and never executes an unsupported instruction.

question_patterns: What happens if you rerun the same Dart program with --target-unknown-cpu?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With --target-unknown-cpu, the same program prints 42 successfully instead of crashing.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It crashes at the same instruction even with --target-unknown-cpu.

question_patterns: Can you run the trace-cpuid Dart build and share whether SSE4.1 is detected?
What CPU features does --trace-cpuid report on the affected machines?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The traces for the affected AMD Athlon/Phenom and Intel Core 2 processors report SSE2 support but 'sse41? no'. The normal floor test still crashes afterward.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: CPU tracing reports SSE4.1 support and the instruction executes correctly outside Flutter.

edges.comment: Thread c47-c67: targeted Dart tests reduced the Flutter failure to SSE4.1 instruction generation. The engineer inferred that JIT CPU restrictions had a hole: the VM emitted roundsd even after detecting that the processor lacked SSE4.1. Results from multiple affected users are merged.

question_patterns: Can you upgrade to Flutter 3.19.5 with Dart 3.3.3 and verify the issue on the affected old CPU?
Please test the stable hotfix release and confirm whether project creation and builds now work.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Flutter 3.19.5 stable with Dart 3.3.3 works on the affected old processors; users can create, build, and run projects again.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Flutter 3.19.5 still exits with -1073741795 on the same affected processors.

question_patterns: Does a Windows build complete, and does the ceil reproduction execute correctly after the hotfix?
Can you also verify the related floating-point sample on Windows?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The Windows executable builds and runs, and the test prints the expected ceil result of 1016. Users also confirmed successful web and Android runs.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Windows build and ceil sample work; the user did not additionally test Android.

edges.comment: Thread c78-c86: the fix shipped in Flutter 3.19.5 and was tested by affected users on old hardware. Windows builds and the related floating-point sample were explicitly verified before closure.

solution.intent: Use the current Flutter stable hotfix containing the Dart VM CPU-restriction correction, so JIT-compiled Flutter tooling does not emit SSE4.1 instructions on processors that report no SSE4.1 support.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade to Flutter 3.19.5 stable, which includes Dart 3.3.3 and the fix preventing the JIT from using SSE4.1 roundsd on unsupported old x86-64 CPUs. Re-run flutter create and a Windows build, and only consider the issue resolved after both succeed on the affected machine.

edges.comment: Resolution from c63-c86: Dart fixed the missing JIT CPU restriction, the correction was cherry-picked into Dart 3.3.3 and released through Flutter 3.19.5 stable, and affected users verified successful builds. Older Flutter 3.16.x releases were not separately hotfixed because only the current stable receives hotfixes.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the true root cause: the Dart VM's JIT CPU-feature restrictions allowed an SSE4.1 instruction such as roundsd to be generated even when CPUID reported that the old x86-64 processor lacked SSE4.1, causing the Flutter tool to terminate with illegal-instruction exit code -1073741795/3221225501.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: releases through Flutter 3.13.9 worked, affected 3.16+ releases failed across platforms, affected users had old CPUs without SSE4.1, the normal Dart floor test crashed, --target-unknown-cpu printed 42, and CPUID tracing reported no SSE4.1.
Must not settle on the falsified generic MSB8066/CMake remedies or SDK reinstallation: the reporter tried both without resolving the failure.
Must direct the user to Flutter 3.19.5 or a newer stable release containing Dart 3.3.3 or the equivalent CPU-restriction fix; it must not imply that Flutter 3.16.x received the hotfix.
Must require verification on affected hardware, including successful project creation or build execution, before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical Flutter developer on older Windows hardware. Comfortable installing multiple SDK versions, checking out Git commits, running verbose commands and supplied diagnostic programs, and sharing detailed console output; deeper VM and CPU-instruction analysis comes from engineers and other affected users folded into the simulated user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, patient, and evidence-driven. Provides exact version comparisons and logs, follows detailed reproduction instructions, and asks for concrete next steps when generic troubleshooting fails.
